name: Decline Plate-Loaded Reverse-Grip Press
description: A decline press using a plate-loaded chest press machine with the hands in a supinated (palms-up, reverse) grip. The reverse grip on the decline angle creates a unique pressing vector that shifts significant tension to the clavicular pectoralis major despite the decline body position, while also increasing biceps brachii involvement as a secondary mover. This unusual combination can overcome training plateaus and add variety to lower-chest training.

execution.starting_position: Sit in a plate-loaded chest press machine set to the decline angle setting. Grip the handles with palms facing upward (supinated grip) rather than the standard overhand grip. Feet secured. Machine loaded appropriately.
execution.setup_instructions: Only use this variation if the machine's handle design allows a comfortable supinated grip without wrist strain. Set the decline angle on the machine. Use less weight than standard grip pressing.
steps: Step 1: Sit in the machine with a supinated grip, handles loaded at chest level.
Step 2: Press the handles forward/out along the machine's guided arc, maintaining the supinated wrist position.
Step 3: Fully extend the arms to the end of the machine's range.
Step 4: Return under control, letting the weight stack descend fully before the next rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale before the press, exhale during the pressing movement.
common_mistakes: Wrist discomfort due to forcing a supinated grip on a machine not designed for it — stop if wrists hurt
Using the same weight as standard grip — the supinated position typically requires 10–20% less load
Rotating forearms mid-rep back to a neutral position
safety_considerations: If the machine handles do not support a comfortable supinated grip, do not force this variation
Start with light weight to assess wrist comfort in the reverse grip position
Secure feet or use the machine's foot support as decline orientation requires
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full range of the machine from fully loaded to full extension.
coaching_cues: Palms face up the entire time — the supinated grip is what makes this unique
Press from the chest, not the arms — the biceps stabilize but the pecs drive
